'''Nikhil Srivastava''' is an associate professor of Mathematics at [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In July 2014, he was named a recipient of the [[George Pólya Prize|Pólya Prize]] with [[Adam Marcus (mathematician)|Adam Marcus]] and [[Daniel Spielman]].

==Early life and education==
Nikhil Srivastava was born New Delhi, India. He attended [[Union College]] in Schenectady, New York, graduating summa cum laude with a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics and computer science in 2005. He received a PhD in computer science from [[Yale University]] in 2010 (his dissertation was called "Spectral Sparsification and Restricted Invertibility").

==Awards==
In 2013, together with [[Adam Marcus (mathematician)|Adam Marcus]] and [[Daniel Spielman]], he provided a positive solution to the [[Kadison–Singer problem]],<ref>{{citation|title= Interlacing families I: Bipartite Ramanujan graphs of all degrees | year=2015 | volume=182 | issue=1 | pages=307–325 | last1 = Marcus | first1 = Adam W. |last2 = Spielman |first2=Daniel A. |last3 = Srivastava |first3 =Nikhil | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]] | arxiv=1304.4132|doi = 10.4007/annals.2015.182.1.7}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title= Interlacing Families II: Mixed Characteristic Polynomials and the Kadison–Singer problem | year=2015 | volume=182 | issue=1 | pages=327–350 | last1 = Marcus | first1 = Adam W. |last2 = Spielman |first2=Daniel A. |last3 = Srivastava |first3 =Nikhil | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]] | arxiv=1306.3969|doi = 10.4007/annals.2015.182.1.8| s2cid=17580893 }}</ref> a result that was awarded the 2014 [[George Pólya Prize|Pólya Prize]].

He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2015-05-15|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> He jointly won the 2021 Michael and Sheila Held Prize along with two others for solving long-standing questions on the Kadison-Singer problem and on Ramanujan graphs.[https://web.archive.org/web/20210201143140/https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/diaspora/indian-mathematician-nikhil-srivastava-wins-michael-and-sheila-held-prize-202075]

In 2022 The Ciprian Foias Prize in Operator Theory was awarded to Adam Marcus, Daniel Spielman, and  Srivastava for their notable work in Operator Theory that was published in the preceding six years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ciprian Foias Prize in Operator Theory |url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=48 |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=2021-12-04 |title=Indian-American mathematician Nikhil Srivastava among 3 selected for inaugural Ciprian Foias Prize |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/indian-american-mathematician-nikhil-srivastava-among-3-selected-for-inaugural-ciprian-foias-prize/article37840306.ece |access-date=2024-01-05 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>
